did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezekiel is instructed to direct his prophecy to the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them, not only against the inhabitants of the land.
Did you know? The prophecy describes the mountains of Israel, the hills, ravines, and valleys as places where the sword will come, and where the high places of worship will be destroyed.
Did you know? Among the objects of worship to be destroyed in this chapter are the altars, high places, idols, and incense altars.
Did you know? Ezekiel says that the corpses of the Israelites will be laid before their idols, and their bones scattered around the altars.
Did you know? Alongside the destruction, the prophecy promises that some survivors will escape the sword and be scattered among the nations and countries.
Did you know? The survivors will remember the Lord in the lands of their exile, acknowledge their sins, and loathe themselves because of the evil and abominations they have committed.
Did you know? Ezekiel is instructed to express his shock by clapping his hands and stamping his feet before describing the punishment of the house of Israel.
Did you know? The chapter presents three ways of dying: those far away will die of plague, those nearby will fall by the sword, and those who remain and are besieged will die of famine.
Did you know? The places of worship are described as hills, mountain peaks, green trees, and spreading terebinths—and there the slain will be found around the idols and altars.
Did you know? At the end of the chapter, the land is described as desolate and devastated in all its settlements, so that the people will know that the Lord is God.
